## Why it works

The most-liked comments quote his jokes and his danger: "That's it. No more using my body as capacitor" with "Famous last words" (8.6K likes, a line from the part with no English captions), "I'll make you learn things, one way or another" (2.1K and 1.9K likes in two comments, one adding "This if the first time i got threatened with knowledge"), and "As an Electrical Engineer, every time he does something that's about to shock him, I have actual anxiety" (1.9K likes). Fewer thank the idea itself: "It's amazing that LEDs use such a low amount of power that they can partly turn on from some random voltage from the environment." (730 likes) and a one-line summary, "LED lights are SO INSANELY EFFICIENT that now you can power it just by rubbing your sock on a carpet" (70 likes). So the views come from the personality and the near-misses; the useful part for us is the idea the 730-like comment names. The opening reaches the problem in 16 seconds after a joke and a subscribe line; the captioned part runs at about 182 words a minute. What viewers did after: mostly joke back; some suggest uses (an LED on an anti-static strap, 285 likes).
